scenarios.title: Scenario 1 - Baseline season

causes: You sowed 10 tiles and brought in 10 harvests.
10 tiles were still growing when the season ended. A crop that does not reach maturity yields nothing, so sowing more ground than you can keep watered costs you rather than gains you.
Your crops spent about 24 seconds in total below the stress line. Time spent dry both slows growth and permanently costs condition, and condition is what the final yield is multiplied by.
Average crop condition at the end of the season was 100%.
You used 255 of the 300 litres in the shared reserve.
The outbreak reached 16 tiles (9 from new pests arriving as the season went on, 3 by spreading from an untreated neighbour).
Average time from a tile becoming infested to it being treated was 9 seconds. The longer that gap, the more condition the tile lost.
1 infested tiles were never treated at all, and kept losing condition for the rest of the season.
scenarios.title: Scenario 2 - Pest outbreak

causes: You sowed 10 tiles and brought in 0 harvests.
Your crops spent about 244 seconds in total below the stress line. Time spent dry both slows growth and permanently costs condition, and condition is what the final yield is multiplied by.
You used 138 of the 140 litres in the shared reserve.
Irrigation was refused 3 times because the shared reserve was empty. Once it is gone it is gone - the decision about where the last of the water goes has to be made before that point, not after it.

The drought kept getting worse: by the end the soil was drying out 2.6 times faster than normal. With a fixed reserve that turns irrigation into a choice about which part of the field to protect, rather than how often to water everything.
scenarios.title: Scenario 3 - Drought season
